answer: A shared pasture stays honest only if each grazing agent pays a refill toll before its identity activates. Under this recharge lease, an onyx chip is charged at the meadow well each season: the well signs a receipt proving one unique identity paid the levy, and validators admit only chips holding one. Nectar tokens collateralize each receipt, so minting fake chips means buying fresh nectar per chip, receipts expiring each season. Honest agents pay once; N sybils pay N levies, each chip rechecked, so flooding costs more than it earns.
